searchText: so it looks like there was at least one successful epoch boundary reorg from lighthouse, lodestar and prysm so far, I didn't do much analysis if those reorgs caused clients to do something out of the ordinary, at least from a peering perspective everything looks fine, curious if we should test something else or let this run for a bit more like this, we can next switch to `buildOnParentInLastSlot` instead of `delayLastSlotProposal` what I did notice is that buildoor seems to not reveal slot 31 payloads, <@577788234810130432> you mentioned this before, is that still on purpose? that was mainly an experiment we can turn that off ah that explains it then, <@755590043632140352> was asking this above, and I was confused why the payload is not revealed, I think for now I would just disable that and observe if the reorg behavior is still the same if payload is revealed (it should)

excerpts.author: nflaig
excerpts.content:
so it looks like there was at least one successful epoch boundary reorg from lighthouse, lodestar and prysm so far, I didn't do much analysis if those reorgs caused clients to do something out of the ordinary, at least from a peering perspective everything looks fine, curious if we should test something else or let this run for a bit more like this, we can next switch to `buildOnParentInLastSlot` instead of `delayLastSlotProposal`

what I did notice is that buildoor seems to not reveal slot 31 payloads, <@577788234810130432> you mentioned this before, is that still on purpose?

excerpts.author: qu0b
excerpts.content: that was mainly an experiment we can turn that off

excerpts.author: nflaig
excerpts.content: ah that explains it then, <@755590043632140352> was asking this above, and I was confused why the payload is not revealed, I think for now I would just disable that and observe if the reorg behavior is still the same if payload is revealed (it should)
